_comment: Cardinal number words and the quantity each names, for the counting-picture
production card (tunatale-elrj). A number word is the one word class with a
perfect, unambiguous picture — the quantity itself — so it must not take the
closed-class cloze route its `Word class` of `determinative` (UPOS DET) would
otherwise send it down.
`values` lists EVERY cardinal the deck carries, including ones outside the
renderable range. That is deliberate: the range cut-off lives in one place,
app/cards/number_image.py::MAX_RENDERABLE, so this file stays a plain
vocabulary and never a second copy of the policy. null (0) and tusen (1000)
are here to record that they ARE numbers and were considered.
`values` must be injective — no two surfaces may name the same quantity,
AFTER `exclude` is applied — the picture is keyed on the value alone, and two
renderable words sharing one picture is exactly the duplicate-image ambiguity
the pre-stage's digest guard exists to prevent. That is why `sju` (the other
spelling of 7) is absent: the deck carries `syv`, and both would be renderable
and would collide. `en` and `ene` may both carry 1 because both are excluded.
A test enforces this.
`exclude` is for words that HAVE a cardinal value but must not be pictured:
en   — 'one' and the indefinite article 'a/an'. A picture of one apple is
equally a picture of 'an apple'. It is already curated into
function_words.json's `include`, and stays a cloze.
ene  — 'one (of two)': a contrastive sense no countable set can express.
halvannen ('one and a half') is in neither map: it is not a cardinal, and the
renderer has no representation for a fraction.
